newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Nov 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Nov 12.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- DOMINION CALLS FOR E MIDLANDS TALKS

Dominion Resources, the Virginia-based utility company, yesterday called for a first meeting with East Midlands Electricity's board after deciding over the weekend that it would pursue its plans for a bid of 1.25 billion pounds stg. It is thought that the meeting could come as early as today, although no appointment has been set.
-- FIRST CHOICE HOLIDAYS' CHIEF QUITS

Francis Baron resigned yesterday as chief executive of First Choice Holidays. The abrupt decision came after his three executive directors secretly complained to the board over the deterioration in their working relationship with him. They claimed that they were unable to continue working with him. Baron, who joined as chief executive three years ago is to receive 640,000 pounds stg compensation for his loss of office.
-- CAPITAL IN 51 MILLION POUNDS DEAL FOR MY KINDA TOWN

Capital Radio revealed a 51 million pounds stg deal to buy My Kinda Town which includes the Henry J Bean and Chicago Pizza Pie Factory restaurant chain. The company defended its radical shift of strategy, saying that it is good at creating entertainment and moving entertainment on. The acquisition at 190p a share marks a far more extensive move into the themed restaurants market than had been expected.
THE TIMES
-- BAe WINS 1 BILLION POUNDS AUSTRALIAN HAWK TRAINERS CONTRACT

British Aerospace has won a 1 billion pounds stg contract to supply Hawk training aircraft to the Australian air force. The contract was won over competition from Italian and American companies on the basis of BAe building new production facilities in Australia. The first 12 Hawks will be built in Britain with the remaining 28 to be manufactured in Australia.
-- LABOUR TOUGHENS INFLATION STANCE

The opposition Labour Party insisted yesterday that in government it would meet a 2.5 percent inflation target in the medium term. In a speech to business leaders at the Confederation of British Industry's annual conference, Gordon Brown, the Shadow Chancellor, insisted that Labour would have a target for low and stable inflation and would match that of its European competitors and not just talk tough as the Tories are doing.
-- BAA PLANS TO LAND BIGGER SHARE OF DUTY-FREE MARKET

BAA, the airports group, has plans to increase the size of its duty-free retailing business by 100 per cent over the next five years. The group has launched World Duty Free, a new subsidiary aimed at taking a bigger share of the world-wide market in tax-free sales to travellers. BAA plans to expand the business through acquisitions and joint ventures, and would take over the duty-free shops in its airports next year.
THE GUARDIAN
-- LAZARDS FRAUD CASE COLLAPSES

A fraud case investigated by the City of London Police, collapsed yesterday when Lazard Brothers, the victim of the fraud, handed fresh material to the public prosecutors on Friday. The details of the collapse are yet to emerge but after the new evidence was presented the Crown's position was made untenable. The case against a former Lazards junior telex clerk was dropped and there is no sign that anyone will now face trial over the alleged defrauding of Lazards of 4 million pounds stg in September 1992.
-- CLARKE 'MUST RAISE RATES'

The governor of the Bank of England, Eddie George, yesterday insisted at an international meeting of central bankers in Basle, that Kenneth Clarke, the Chancellor, will be forced to raise base rates to guarantee his inflation target. He said that Clarke's recent decision to raise base rates to 6 per cent would only limit the size of another increase if the 2.5 per cent inflation target was to be met.
-- TELEKOM FLOAT INCREASED TO MEET DEMAND

Due to unexpectedly high demand from the German public, Deutsche Telekom has increased the size of its public offer by 20 percent. The number of shares available have been increased from 575 million to 690 million. The move could raise an extra 1.4 billion pounds stg. The decision to boost the size of the offer is seen as a victory for the Bonn government which has been trying to get the German public to invest more in shares. THE INDEPENDENT
-- CARPETBAGGERS CASH IN ON A&L LOOPHOLE

"Carpetbaggers" whom the Alliance & Leicester Building Society tried to shut out of a free shares handout when the society floats on the stock market, are likely to benefit from payouts worth thousands of pounds stg instead, because of a legal loophole. The society planned to give each of its members a fixed amount of 250 shares worth around 1000 pounds stg. Policyholders who joined after the society's 31 December 1995 cut-off date for new accounts are not entitled to free shares after conversion. But accounts opened between 31 December and 16 January 1996 still give all other membership rights. Those accounts are still entitled to a cash share of the society's assets with payouts based on about 11 per cent of the amount in an individual's account.
-- STRONG POUND HALVES BRITISH STEEL PROFIT

British Steel said yesterday that it may be forced to speed up redundancy plans to remain competitive against European producers if the pound strengthened any further. Chairman and chief executive, Sir Brian Moffat reported interim profits of 262 million pounds stg from 550 million pounds stg, and said that because of the pound's strength, the group's cost competitiveness had been eroded while competitors had been advantaged.
-- EMAP PROFIT OF 51 MILLION POUNDS PUTS FEUD IN BACK SEAT

Emap, the media company, yesterday announced interim profits rose 34 per cent to 50.6 million pounds stg. The company, who is in the middle of a boardroom feud, also booked a pre-tax profit gain of 113.5 million pounds stg from the sale of its newspaper and printing businesses to Johnston Press.
